blocks.content: The decision of the Chairman or the Speaker regarding disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is subject to judicial review.

headers: Rule for Joining a Political Party
rows: Cannot join any political party after the election.
Joins any political party at any time after being elected.
Allowed to join a political party within the first 6 months of taking their seat.
Joins any political party AFTER the expiry of 6 months.

items: An independent elected member becomes disqualified if he or she joins any political party after the election.
A nominated member becomes disqualified if he or she joins any political party AFTER the expiry of six months from taking their seat.

Following the landmark Kihoto Hollohan case (1992), the Presiding Officer functions as a tribunal while deciding defection cases, making the decision subject to judicial review on grounds of mala fides or perversity.
The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 recognized only mergers (requiring 2/3rd majority) and abolished the exemption previously allowed for splits (1/3rd majority).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Anti-Defection Law was added to the Constitution by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985 via the Tenth Schedule.
Disqualification occurs if a member voluntarily gives up party membership or votes/abstains contrary to party direction without prior permission.
The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 eliminated the provision that protected defection in case of a one-third split in a political party.
A disqualification exception exists if at least two-thirds of the members of a legislature party agree to merge with another party.
The Speaker or Chairman of the House serves as the deciding authority, and their decision is subject to judicial review following the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992).
